summary: Shailendra Bhandare works in Indology and history and archaeology. He has held positions as curator at the British Museum, a fellow at the Fitzwilliam Museum, Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022), and Fellow at St Cross College (attested 2022).

Shaman Hatley specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1999–2007) under Shrikant S. Bahulkar, Ludo Rocher, and Harunaga Isaacson, later teaching at Concordia University and chairing Asian studies at UMass Boston.
Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts at McMaster University, where she studied under MA supervisor James A. Benn and teachers Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Shanshan Jia works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied as a doctoral student in Indology at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson (attested 2015, 2026), where she also served as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Shaoyong Ye is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan by 2009, subsequently serving there as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2014) under the supervision of Steven D. Goodman.

Sharon Salzberg (b. 1952) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at the University at Buffalo and under teachers including Anagarika Munindra, Satya Narayan Goenka, and Dipa Ma. She co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911–1964) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA 1935, PhD 1939), he later served as a Lecturer at the University of Calcutta (attested 1950).

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, Canterbury (MA under Paul Harrison), and UCLA (PhD 2006 under Gregory Schopen). He serves as Associate Professor at McMaster University and Research Fellow at IIBS (attested 2026).

Shechen Gyaltsab (1871–1926) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught prominent figures such as Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (b. 1966) is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff (b. 1944) studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held academic posts at Cornell University (~1978–1998) and Harvard University (~1998).

Shek-Wing Tam (1935–2024) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Ying-Kuang Chu, and Yui Chi Lau. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America and held posts at Renmin and Tsinghua Universities.

Sheldon Pollock (b. 1948) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, University of Chicago, and Columbia University, and served as General Editor of the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University, taught at Shandao Temple and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and founded Dharma Drum Mountain.

Shenghai Li specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) under Donald R. Davis Jr., having also studied with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe, and Ram Shankar Tripathi.

Shenpen Hookham (b. 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Reading and the University of Oxford (D.Phil under Michael M. Broido), as well as under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.

Shenphen Nangwa (1871–1927) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy figure who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Önpo Tenzin Norbu. He taught at Dzogchen Monastery and founded Dzongsar Monastery, serving as the first khenpo of its shedra in 1918.

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar educated at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries. He founded the Buddhist Association of China, served as its president (~1953–1966), and was Dean of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Sherry B. Ortner (b. 1941) works in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Bryn Mawr College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan, she held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan, and UCLA.
